title: AI Solution Architect (m/w/d)

description:
About the role

0G is hiring its first dedicated DevOps engineer to own our cloud platform end to end: infrastructure, deployments, networking, security hygiene and cost. Today that work is spread across several developers.

Our platform runs on five providers: Google Cloud, Alibaba Cloud, AWS, Cloudflare and Vercel. It includes:

  • Validator, seed, RPC, and archive nodes for our mainnet and testnet

  • Confidential-computing (TEE) workloads, GPU machines and storage nodes

  • Kubernetes clusters and managed databases

  • A global RPC load balancer at the edge, and our web apps

All together, that is more than 200 virtual machines. You will be the person who knows what runs where, why it runs there, and what it costs.

What you'll own

You own the platform, from the network edge to the bill.

  • Cloud operations: provisioning, upgrades, capacity and the full resource lifecycle on Google Cloud, Alibaba Cloud and AWS. That includes rightsizing and releasing what nobody uses.

  • Kubernetes: run, upgrade and scale our clusters. Keep them on supported versions and design node pools, autoscaling and Spot capacity.

  • Blockchain node fleet: operate validator, sentry, seed, RPC and archive nodes, including peering topology, snapshots, sync and client upgrades.

  • Networking and edge: VPC design, load balancers, DNS, Cloudflare Workers, Tunnels and WAF, and keeping internet egress deliberate and cheap.

  • Infrastructure as code and CI/CD: every environment defined in Terraform or Pulumi. You design and run CI/CD on Jenkins or an equivalent such as GitHub Actions or GitLab CI, covering builds, tests, security scans and releases from commit to production, with no manual steps.

  • Observability and on-call: metrics, logs, alerts and dashboards, including control of metric cardinality. You also run incident response and write the postmortems.

  • Security and access: least-privilege IAM across every provider, secrets management, and no databases or admin ports open to the internet.

  • Cost management: billing exports, budgets and alerts, tagging, a monthly cost review and commitment planning.

  • Developer enablement: templates, preview environments, documentation and support for the engineers who ship on the platform.

Our stack

Kubernetes: GKE, EKS, Helm, Ingress and Gateway API, autoscaling, RBAC, network policies

Networking: TCP/IP, subnets and CIDR, routing, NAT, L4 and L7 load balancers, DNS, TLS, firewalls, VPC peering

Google Cloud: Compute Engine, GKE, Cloud SQL, Cloud Run, IAM, Cloud Monitoring, billing export to BigQuery

Infrastructure as code: Terraform, Pulumi

CI/CD and containers: Jenkins or an equivalent (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI), Argo CD, Docker and BuildKit, container registries

Observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Cloud Monitoring, CloudWatch, Alibaba CloudMonitor

Linux: Systems administration, systemd, disks and filesystems, performance debugging

Alibaba Cloud: ECS, VPC, NLB and ALB, ESSD disks, RDS, PolarDB, SAE, Cloud Firewall

AWS: EC2, EKS, RDS, ALB and NLB, Route 53, S3, Organizations

Cloudflare: DNS, Workers, Tunnels, WAF and rate limiting, Zero Trust

Databases (operations): PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, managed Kafka

Blockchain nodes: CometBFT-based chains, reth and other EVM clients, P2P networking

Vercel: Projects, builds, ISR, team access

Confidential computing: Intel TDX virtual machines on Google Cloud and Alibaba Cloud

Must-haves

  • We want 5+ years in DevOps, SRE or platform roles, including 3+ years running production Kubernetes and owning CI/CD pipelines.

Kubernetes, in depth

  • Upgrading control planes and node pools with no downtime, and keeping clusters on supported versions.

  • Scheduling: requests and limits, affinity, taints and tolerations, priority, and eviction under node pressure.

  • Autoscaling with the HPA, cluster autoscaler or Karpenter, plus Spot or preemptible node pools for non-critical work.

  • Networking inside the cluster: CNI, Services, Ingress or Gateway API, network policies, and DNS within the cluster.

  • Security: RBAC, Pod Security, workload identity, and secrets that never sit in plain environment variables.

  • Stateful workloads: StatefulSets, persistent volumes and CSI drivers, and backup and restore.

  • Packaging and delivery with Helm or Kustomize, ideally through GitOps with Argo CD or Flux.

  • Debugging a failing pod, node or rollout from events, logs and metrics.

CI/CD, in depth

  • Pipeline design: you have built and run production CI/CD on Jenkins or an equivalent (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI, Tekton). Pipelines are defined as code in a Jenkinsfile or workflow YAML, with shared libraries and reusable templates.

  • CI platform operations: running Jenkins controllers with ephemeral agents on Kubernetes, or self-hosted runners. That includes plugin and version upgrades, credential handling, and scaling build capacity.

  • Build pipelines: multi-service and monorepo builds with caching and parallel stages, and versioned artifacts. Container images built with Docker, BuildKit or Kaniko, including multi-architecture images, image scanning, SBOMs and signing.

  • Deployment pipelines: promotion from dev to staging to production with approvals and quality gates, plus blue-green, canary and fast rollback. GitOps with Argo CD or Flux, and database migrations as part of a release.

  • Infrastructure pipelines: Terraform or Pulumi plan and apply from CI, with policy checks and drift detection.

  • Pipeline security: short-lived credentials through OIDC federation or a secrets vault instead of long-lived keys, least-privilege deploy roles, and protected branches.

  • Release engineering for our chain: building and publishing node binaries and images, and coordinating rolling upgrades across validator and RPC fleets.

  • Delivery health: you track build time, build cost, flaky tests and DORA metrics (deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, time to restore), and you cut wasted builds with ignore rules and caching.

Networking fundamentals

  • TCP/IP, subnetting and CIDR, routing, NAT, and the difference between L4 and L7 load balancing.

  • DNS, TLS and certificates, firewalls and security groups.

  • Private connectivity: VPC design, peering, private endpoints, and keeping internal traffic off public IPs.

  • Troubleshooting with dig, curl, mtr and tcpdump, and understanding what internet egress costs.

Also required

  • Production experience on at least two of Google Cloud, AWS and Alibaba Cloud, and willingness to learn the third quickly.

  • Terraform or Pulumi in production, plus scripting in Bash and in Python or Go.

  • A track record of cutting a cloud bill with data, through rightsizing, cleanup or commitments.

  • A security-first habit with production credentials, and clear written communication.

Nice to have

  • Running blockchain nodes in production, such as CometBFT validators and sentries, EVM archive or RPC nodes, and snapshot pipelines.

  • Cloudflare Workers, Tunnels and Zero Trust at scale.

  • Alibaba Cloud on the international site, including its billing and support model.

  • Confidential computing (Intel TDX) and GPU workloads.

  • CKA or CKS certification, a FinOps certification, or experience moving a team between CI systems, such as Jenkins to GitHub Actions.

  • Go or Rust, enough to read and patch the services you operate.

What we offer

  • Purpose: The opportunity to contribute to making AI a public good

  • Growth: A self-directed environment where you can take initiative to shape your role and career

  • Compensation: Market-competitive compensation including, for most roles, exposure to pre-launch tokens

In addition, 0G Labs is committed to the health and well being of all of our team members. To that end, we provide reimbursements towards a holistic set of experiences and courses:

  • Core self: Transcendental Meditation

  • Mind: Landmark Education

  • Emotion: Art of Communication

  • Presence: Speech Coach

  • Body: Fitness, gym and exercise memberships/classes

title: Senior DevOps Engineer

description:
Betriebliche Steuern sind kompliziert – Steuerberatung muss es nicht sein. Für die meisten Unternehmen bedeutet sie bis heute Papierstapel, lange E-Mail-Verläufe und Warten. Das wollen wir grundlegend ändern.

Bei b'steuern verbinden wir Steuerberatung, Software und KI von Anfang an miteinander. Unser Ziel ist nicht, eine klassische Steuerkanzlei einfach digitaler zu machen. Wir definieren neu, was Steuerberatung bedeutet: mit KI-Agenten, die ganze Arbeitsabläufe eigenständig übernehmen, und Software, die Menschen genau dort einbindet, wo sie gebraucht werden.

Dafür reicht es nicht, bestehende Prozesse einfach in Software zu übersetzen. Wir müssen verstehen, welche Arbeit überhaupt noch von Menschen erledigt werden muss, was KI-Agenten eigenständig übernehmen können und wie daraus zuverlässige, skalierbare Systeme entstehen.

Als Product Engineer findest du die Probleme, die es wert sind, gelöst zu werden – und löst sie von Anfang bis Ende. Du arbeitest direkt mit unserem Steuerteam zusammen, verstehst die Herausforderungen im Arbeitsalltag und entwickelst eigenständig Lösungen: von der ersten Idee über Backend, Frontend und KI-Integration bis zum produktiven Einsatz.

Dabei bist du Teil unseres Engineering-Teams und gestaltest mit, wie wir Software und autonome KI-Systeme entwickeln, die mit unserem Unternehmen wachsen.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Die Arbeit unseres Steuerteams neu denken. Du arbeitest direkt mit den Menschen zusammen, die unsere Software täglich nutzen. Du verstehst ihre Prozesse, identifizierst Engpässe und entwickelst Lösungen, die ihre Arbeit grundlegend einfacher, schneller und besser machen.

  • Features end-to-end verantworten. Du wartest nicht auf fertige Anforderungen oder detaillierte Tickets. Du findest heraus, welches Problem gelöst werden sollte, entwickelst eine Lösung und setzt sie über den gesamten Stack hinweg um. Fertig bist du erst, wenn sie im Arbeitsalltag tatsächlich funktioniert und einen Unterschied macht.

  • KI-Agenten in echte Arbeitsabläufe integrieren. Unsere Agenten übernehmen zunehmend ganze Prozesse – von der Verarbeitung von Dokumenten bis zur eigenständigen Bearbeitung komplexer Aufgaben. Du entwickelst die Systeme, Schnittstellen und Workflows, mit denen KI-Agenten zuverlässig zusammenarbeiten und Menschen dort einbinden, wo sie gebraucht werden.

  • Unsere Softwareprodukte weiterentwickeln. Du baust Features für unser Kundenportal und unsere internen Werkzeuge – von intuitiven Oberflächen über Datenmodelle bis zur Businesslogik dahinter.

  • Unser Engineering-Team verstärken. Du bringst deine technische Perspektive in Architekturentscheidungen ein, verbesserst bestehende Systeme und hilfst uns, auch bei schnellem Wachstum zuverlässige und wartbare Software zu entwickeln.

  • Schnell lernen und iterieren. Du bringst Ideen früh in den Livebetrieb, holst dir direktes Feedback und verbesserst deine Lösungen kontinuierlich. Du weißt, wann ein pragmatischer Ansatz ausreicht und wann es sich lohnt, technisch tiefer zu gehen.

Das bringst du mit

  • Du bist ein starker Software Engineer. Du hast anspruchsvolle Software entwickelt, die tatsächlich im Produktivbetrieb eingesetzt wird. Du verstehst nicht nur, wie man Features implementiert, sondern auch, wie man zuverlässige Systeme entwirft, debuggt und weiterentwickelt.

  • Du fühlst dich im gesamten Stack wohl. Du hast fundierte Erfahrung mit moderner Softwareentwicklung – von Backend-Logik, Datenbanken und APIs bis zu Frontend-Anwendungen. Du musst nicht jede Technologie kennen, kannst dich aber schnell in neue Systeme einarbeiten. Erfahrung mit TypeScript, React oder Python ist besonders hilfreich.

  • Du denkst in Problemen, nicht in Tickets. Du willst verstehen, warum etwas gebaut werden sollte, bevor du über die technische Umsetzung nachdenkst. Du kannst unklare Anforderungen selbst strukturieren, pragmatische Entscheidungen treffen und Verantwortung für das Ergebnis übernehmen.

  • Du denkst AI-native. Du hinterfragst ständig, wie du mit KI besser und schneller Software entwickeln kannst, experimentierst mit neuen Ansätzen und teilst erfolgreiche Workflows mit dem Team. Gleichzeitig hast du das technische Verständnis, um Qualität, Sicherheit und Wartbarkeit deiner Lösungen selbst zu beurteilen.

  • Du baust schnell, aber nicht leichtfertig. Du kannst pragmatisch vorgehen und schnell funktionierende Lösungen ausliefern. Gleichzeitig erkennst du, wann Zuverlässigkeit, saubere Architektur und technische Qualität entscheidend sind.

  • Du übernimmst Verantwortung. Du brauchst keine fertig priorisierte Aufgabenliste. Du findest selbst heraus, was wichtig ist, treibst Themen eigenständig voran und bleibst dran, bis das Problem wirklich gelöst ist.

  • Du diskutierst offen und konstruktiv. Du vertrittst deine Meinung, gibst klares Feedback und lässt dich vom besseren Argument überzeugen.

  • Du sprichst sehr gut Deutsch und fließend Englisch und lebst in Berlin oder bist bereit, hierherzuziehen.

Erfahrung mit KI-Agenten, B2B-Software, komplexen Geschäftsprozessen oder in einem anspruchsvollen Start-up ist ein Plus. Ein bestimmter Abschluss, ein klassischer Werdegang oder eine bestimmte Anzahl an Berufsjahren sind dagegen keine Voraussetzung. Entscheidend ist, was du bereits gebaut hast, wie gut du technische Probleme lösen kannst und wie du an neue Herausforderungen herangehst.

Passt die Rolle zu dir?

Du fühlst dich bei uns wohl, wenn du …

  • genauso gern Operations-Probleme löst, wie du anspruchsvolle Software entwickelst,

  • Freude daran hast, Features von der ersten Idee bis zum produktiven Einsatz selbst zu verantworten,

  • Lust hast, mit AI-Agents völlig neue Arbeitsabläufe und Produkte zu entwickeln,

  • gern direkt mit Nutzern sprichst, statt ausschließlich technische Anforderungen entgegenzunehmen,

  • selbst herausfindest, welches Problem gerade am wichtigsten ist, statt auf eine fertige Aufgabenliste zu warten,

  • hohe technische Ansprüche hast, aber pragmatisch bleibst und lieber früh etwas Funktionierendes auslieferst,

  • offen über deine Arbeit diskutierst und dich vom besseren Argument überzeugen lässt.

Die Rolle passt eher nicht, wenn du …

  • am liebsten klar definierte Tickets abarbeitest und Produktentscheidungen anderen überlässt,

  • dich ausschließlich auf Backend, Frontend oder Infrastruktur spezialisieren möchtest und wenig Interesse am Rest des Produkts hast,

  • lieber an technisch interessanten Problemen arbeitest, unabhängig davon, ob sie einen echten Mehrwert schaffen,

  • feste Prozesse, enge Zuständigkeiten und vollständig ausgearbeitete Anforderungen erwartest,

  • deine Arbeit als erledigt betrachtest, sobald der Code gemerged ist, statt zu prüfen, ob die Lösung im Alltag funktioniert.

Warum b'steuern?

  • Eine Branche neu gestalten: Wir bauen nicht einfach bessere Kanzleisoftware. Wir entwickeln eine neue Art der Steuerberatung, in der Software und autonome KI-Agenten einen großen Teil der Arbeit übernehmen.

  • Software und Kanzlei unter einem Dach: Wir entwickeln unsere Produkte direkt im eigenen Kanzleibetrieb. Du kannst mit den Menschen sprechen, für die du baust, und neue Ideen unmittelbar im Arbeitsalltag testen.

  • Wachstum: Jeden Monat kommen viele neue Mandant dazu. Was du entwickelst, erreicht schnell immer mehr Menschen.

  • Tempo: Wir deployen mehrfach täglich. Manche Features sind zwei Stunden nach der ersten Idee schon im Einsatz.

  • Technische Verantwortung: Du entwickelst nicht nur einzelne Features, sondern gestaltest unsere Systeme, Architektur und Engineering-Praktiken aktiv mit.

  • Flache Strukturen: Wir arbeiten selbstorganisiert. Es zählt das beste Argument, nicht der Titel oder die lauteste Stimme.

  • Kompetitives Gehalt: Wir bieten eine attraktive Vergütung abhängig von Erfahrung, Fähigkeiten und Impact.

  • Arbeitsort: Unser Büro am Hackeschen Markt mit lebendiger Teamkultur. Wir arbeiten 3–5 Tage pro Woche gemeinsam vor Ort.

Deine Bewerbung

Ein Anschreiben brauchst du nicht. Zeig uns lieber etwas, das du selbst gebaut hast und auf das du stolz bist.

Erzähl uns in ein paar Sätzen, welches Problem du gelöst hast, welche technischen Entscheidungen du dabei getroffen hast und welchen Unterschied deine Lösung gemacht hat. Besonders interessiert uns, wo du selbst Verantwortung übernommen hast – von der ersten Idee bis zum produktiven Einsatz.

Wir freuen uns auf dich!

description:
About the Role at RobCo

RobCo is building the category of Autonomous Industrial Robotics and we're doing it fast. We believe that automating the ordinary frees humans to do the extraordinary, and we're building the end-to-end robotics infrastructure to make that possible - hardware, software, and AI in one stack that just works.

 

At RobCo, we don’t just build robots, we are redefining the relationship between hardware and AI. Our end-to-end solutions seamlessly combine advanced, scalable industrial hardware with a central software suite powered by Physical AI to make manufacturing truly autonomous, efficient, and scalable. By delivering field-ready robotic solutions that just work, we empower industrial companies to automate without complexity and successfully solve the global labor shortage.

One controller codebase drives our modular robots, OEM configurations and Alfie, our autonomous industrial robot, so your team's work reaches every robot in the field. Why join RobCo?

description:
Description

QuantumDiamonds is building the world’s first commercial quantum sensing tools for chip failure analysis. As our Research Software Engineering Intern in Pre-Development, you bring our measurement software together. A measurement protocol is the recipe our Quantum Diamond Microscope (QDm) follows for one measurement: how laser, microwaves and camera are sequenced and timed, and how raw camera frames become a magnetic field image of a chip. Our engineers write new protocols whenever they test a new idea, and several backends for running them grew in parallel. You turn them into one shared Python framework that our engineers extend.

The challenge is a framework R&D still uses long after your internship: flexible enough that a new protocol is a day’s work, automated enough that a measurement runs without someone watching it, and structured enough that the next engineer extends it without reading all of it. An experienced colleague from the team mentors you and sets the architecture; you make that trade-off real in code, working with Claude Code every day, as our engineers do.

This is a full-time internship for 6 months, during or after your studies, starting as soon as possible.

Who we are

Founded in 2022 as a spin-off of TU Munich, QD leverages quantum sensors to rapidly capture three-dimensional current maps within multi-layer chips. Our strong, international team of over 70, including physicists, engineers, data scientists, and other experts, works side by side with major semiconductor manufacturers, supporting chip debugging and accelerating yield analysis. Backed by top-tier deep tech investors, semiconductor experts, and strategic public programs, we have ensured long-term stability, shifting from breakthrough to scale - and shaping the next chapter in chip testing.

Why join QuantumDiamonds?

Picture this:

  • Quantum sensors that see inside the most advanced chips on Earth, right where two frontier fields collide.

  • Nobel-Prize physics aimed at real customers with real problems, in production now, not someday.

  • Physicists, data scientists, and engineers building side by side, turning deep science into tools the industry actually runs on.

  • An international team that runs at hard problems for fun, where knowledge moves fast and so do you.

Still unsure about why joining us?

  • You'll get to build a company together with a brilliant and welcoming team on a product that has never been done before.

  • From Day 1, you'll own your own topics end to end and see the direct impact of your work on how the world sees QuantumDiamonds.

  • Our technology is the cutting edge of tomorrow, starting today and not in 10 years.

  • You’ll be part of a high-growth company backed by top-tier investors.

Let’s make the invisible visible!

 
 

What will you do

  • Bring the measurement software of Pre-Development together into one shared Python framework, to a target architecture your mentor defines, and migrate the existing measurement protocols onto it.

  • Keep the CI/CD pipeline on GitHub Actions healthy as the framework grows: tests, linting, packaging, releases.

  • Give first-pass reviews on pull requests from our engineers (tests, conventions, API conformance) before your mentor approves them.

  • Help our engineers extend the stack: new measurement protocols become modules in the framework, and you validate the migrated ones on our QDm systems together with them.

  • Document the framework and hand it over so the team runs it on its own after your internship.

 

What is expected of you

  • Enrolled in or recently graduated from a degree program in computer science, software engineering, computational engineering, physics or electrical engineering with a strong software focus.

  • Available full time for 6 months, starting as soon as possible.

  • Python is your working language: you structure packages, write type hints and tests, and have refactored or consolidated code you did not write.

  • Git and CI are routine for you, and you know how to make hardware-dependent code testable: mocked instruments, recorded data and simulation, with runs on real hardware as a separate stage.

  • AI coding agents are part of how you work, and you check their output the way you check your own.

  • You review code and take review well, you can agree on a common interface with engineers who each prefer their own solution, and you treat your colleagues as your users.

  • Fluent in English. On-site in Munich.

Experience with instrument control or lab automation in Python, with frameworks such as qudi, QCoDeS or PyMeasure, or contributions to open-source projects are a plus, not required. What we want you to bring is the patience to read code you did not write and the discipline to leave it better structured than you found it.

Our benefits

  • Mission: At QD, we’re driven by more than just building great products - we aim to make a lasting difference. Joining us means contributing to meaningful work that goes beyond business as usual.

  • Impact & growth: This is an exciting stage of our journey, and your voice matters. You’ll have the chance to shape our culture, influence key decisions, and grow alongside a company that’s scaling fast.

  • Mentoring: An experienced colleague from the team mentors you throughout your internship.

  • Health & fitness: With a company-sponsored Wellpass membership, you’ll have access to countless gyms, classes, and wellness offers across Germany to stay healthy and active.

  • Team & culture: We believe the best ideas come when we connect outside the office. From regular off-sites to team events, you’ll be part of a collaborative and supportive environment.

  • Well-being & balance: We value rest and recovery. That’s why you’ll enjoy 24 vacation days plus public holidays to recharge and return inspired.

About us

QuantumDiamonds GmbH, headquartered in Munich, Germany, develops and manufactures semiconductor inspection systems based on quantum sensing. Spun out of the Technical University of Munich in 2022, the company uses nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond to map electrical current with micrometer precision inside advanced 2.5D and 3D chip architectures. Nine of the world's ten largest semiconductor manufacturers are engaged with QuantumDiamonds, with systems deployed across Europe, the United States, and Asia. The company is investing €152 million to build the world's first production facility for quantum sensing-based semiconductor inspection tools, supported under the European Chips Act.

description:
Our Global Structure


Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Your job is to make sure every payout and transaction lands with the right person.

We have spent years getting very good at protecting the things a marketplace has always had to protect: checkout fraud, account takeover, courier abuse. But we are no longer only a marketplace. We now issue banking products, lend to merchants, move instant payouts to couriers, and collect cash on the doorstep. Every one of those is a new way for money to leave the platform.

This is a new team, and it owns that surface: fraud wherever money moves through the platform. Who receives it, who lends it, who collects it, and who holds it in a financial account. Think instant payout rails, merchant cash advances, and platform-issued banking and earned-wage products serving millions of couriers and merchants. These are live loss surfaces, and the volume grows with every financial product we launch.

We are now looking for a Backend Engineer (Golang) to build that protection. You will design and ship real-time detection and automated enforcement for our financial products across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo. The work is high-throughput, low-latency, and unusually consequential: a rule you ship on Monday can stop a serious loss by Friday. It is also close to greenfield, so you will be setting the patterns every future financial product inherits on day one.

This role will be based in London, UK as one of the founding engineering roles in our London hub, working closely with our teams in Helsinki and Berlin.

What you'll do:

  • Build and maintain high-throughput, low-latency backend services in Go that score financial events in real time, including payout enrollments, bank account links, credit applications, and account-to-account transfers.
  • Design fraud detection and automated enforcement for our financial products end to end: from signal collection through to the decision that blocks a fraudulent payout.
  • Build on and extend our shared fraud decisioning platform, so signals, rules, and models work across all three of our brands instead of being rebuilt three times.
  • Partner closely with risk analysts, data scientists, and product managers to turn observed fraud patterns into shipped detection, and to know when a rule, a model, or a product change is the right answer.
  • Work across team boundaries with our account security, payments fraud, and financial product teams. We build on their signals rather than rebuild them, so clean interfaces matter.
  • Contribute to architectural discussions and technical decisions as we establish the fraud infrastructure baseline for financial products, with support from senior engineers on the team.
  • Write well-tested, observable code and help the team hold a high quality bar. In fraud, a silent failure is a loss event.

Our expectations:

  • 3 to 6 years of professional software engineering experience, including backend services you have shipped and owned in production.
  • 1+ years of production experience in Golang, or strong experience in another backend language and real enthusiasm for picking Go up quickly.
  • A working understanding of low-latency, high-throughput distributed systems. Real-time decisioning comes with a latency budget, and you are keen to learn to build inside one.
  • Hands-on experience with SQL and/or NoSQL databases, and some exposure to event-driven architectures (Kafka or similar).
  • Willingness to operate what you build, including a share of on-call, with a pragmatic approach to reliability.
  • Uses AI tooling in day-to-day development and can critically evaluate its output for correctness and quality.

Nice to have

  • Experience in fraud, risk, payments, lending, or financial crime, especially money movement fraud, bank account linking fraud, payout abuse, or lending fraud.
  • Experience with rules engines, real-time feature stores, or ML model serving in a decisioning path.
  • Background in Kotlin, Java, Python, or Node.js alongside Go.
  • Familiarity with cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP).
  • Experience working across multiple brands, regions, or regulatory regimes.

What we value

  • A product-oriented mindset. You think beyond the ticket, understand the "why" behind the work, and take a high level of responsibility for outcomes rather than output.
  • Comfort with ambiguity. This is a new team on a new surface; parts of the charter are still being drawn, and you will help draw them.
  • A track record of owning a project or feature end to end, especially in fast-paced environments.
  • Clear and proactive communication, with a collaborative spirit. We work across three companies and several time zones, so we move fast, but we succeed together.
  • An adversarial instinct. The best fraud engineers enjoy thinking like the attacker.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We're committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong.

We believe in equality of opportunity and welcome candidates from all backgrounds regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion, or belief.

If you have a disability or long-term health condition and need support to apply for one of our roles, or require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, you'll have the opportunity to let us know once you've submitted your application. We'll share details on how to request support so we can ensure you have a fair and equitable experience.

If you're excited about making a real impact in a fast-moving marketplace and growing your career alongside ambitious, supportive teams, we'd love to hear from you!

About Wolt

At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we're building the delivery of (almost) everything and you'll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.

Working at Wolt isn't always easy, but it's definitely exciting. Here you'll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You'll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you're a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.

About the Team

Our Infrastructure teams build the foundation that engineers at Wolt, Deliveroo, and DoorDash build on: the compute, cloud, and networking capabilities that enable Engineering teams to develop, deploy, and run services at global scale. The EU Compute team has a specific focus on provisioning, scaling, and the efficient operation of GPU infrastructure for AI and ML workloads. This is an emerging space with plenty of greenfield opportunities.

We're looking for a Staff Engineer to be a hands-on technical leader for this infrastructure work that crosses team and brand boundaries. You'll set direction for the platform, turn complex problems into deliverable plans, write and review production code, and help other engineers make sound decisions. It's an exciting time to join: we're building a global platform and the choices made now will shape how engineers across the company ship for years.

What you'll be doing

You'll own some of the hardest infrastructure problems in the company and make the platform easier to operate and safer to build on. We're determined to build great platform products and user experiences, and you'll be pivotal in making this reality.

Day-to-day in this role you'll:

  • Set technical direction for shared AWS and Kubernetes infrastructure, balancing reliability, security, developer experience, and cost.
  • Lead substantial initiatives from design through rollout and operation, coordinating dependencies and decisions across Wolt, Deliveroo and DoorDash, focusing on workloads targeting GPUs.
  • Evolve Kubernetes clusters, cloud networking, identity, and infrastructure provisioning to support growing and varied workloads.
  • Build reusable Terraform patterns and self-service tooling that help teams provision infrastructure safely and consistently.
  • Improve deployment and operational practices, including GitOps, observability, capacity planning, incident response and recovery.
  • Use production signals and developer feedback to find platform friction, choose where to invest and measure whether changes actually help.
  • Assist with supporting the platform, with deep focus on GPU infrastructure, as well as broad focus on compute in general.
  • Gracefully sunset legacy infrastructure and tooling, and create strategies to reduce toil.
  • Mentor engineers through design reviews, implementation and incidents, raising the quality of infrastructure work across teams.

Our humble expectations

  • Deep experience building and operating Kubernetes and AWS infrastructure in production. Familiarity with GPU workloads and orchestration is a plus.
  • Strong software engineering skills: you use Go, Python or a similar language to build maintainable tools and automation.
  • Experience with infrastructure as code (we use Terraform) and with designing systems that other engineering teams depend on.
  • A track record of leading complex technical work across teams, including architectural decisions, delivery, and operational follow-through. You have the breadth to collaborate and design across team and domain boundaries, and the depth to have hands-on impact.
  • Strong judgment on trade-offs in distributed systems, networking, security, reliability, and cloud cost.
  • Clear communication, and the ability to bring people together around a practical technical direction.

What we offer

  • Scope and influence. Shape infrastructure used globally, while staying close to the engineering. Your work will help product teams ship services with greater ease and confidence.
  • Real problems at global scale. Multi-cluster Kubernetes, AI / ML workloads, cloud networking, GitOps, and progressive delivery across a global company.
  • Autonomy and ownership. Set direction and see it through from design to operation, with the backing of a global engineering organisation spanning Europe and the US.
  • Growth. Room to expand your scope, whether through deeper technical leadership or broader cross-domain influence.
  • Great people. Work with talented engineers and leaders in a diverse, international environment, mentoring and learning from others.

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

We're committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That's why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

Senior Software-Entwickler (m/w/d) – PHP/Symfony & React – Berlin

Der Plan steht, jetzt fehlst du: Bring unsere Software von Legacy-PHP auf Symfony und React.

Auf einen Blick

  • Stack: PHP 8.1 (Legacy) → Symfony · jQuery/Vanilla-JS → React · MySQL/MariaDB, SingleStore · Git, CI/CD

  • Vertrag: unbefristet, Vollzeit

  • Arbeitsmodell: hybrid, 3 Tage Büro / 2 Tage remote

  • Standort: Berlin-Zehlendorf, direkt am S-Bahnhof Zehlendorf (S1)

  • Produkt: Konsentas, ein Termin- und Vorgangsmanagement für Behörden

  • Start: so bald wie möglich oder nach Vereinbarung

Die Rolle

Unser Kernprodukt Konsentas ist über viele Jahre gewachsen, und das sieht man dem Code an. Das Backend läuft auf PHP 8.1 ohne Framework. Im Frontend stehen jQuery und Vanilla-JS neben React, und automatisierte Tests gibt es bisher wenige.

Wohin es gehen soll, ist klar: Das Backend wird schrittweise auf Symfony umgestellt, das Frontend auf React vereinheitlicht. Bis Ende 2027 soll die Migration abgeschlossen sein. Was dafür fehlt, ist kein Plan, sondern Kapazität.

Du triffst eigenständig technische Entscheidungen, bringst dich in Architektur- und Modernisierungsfragen ein und sorgst dafür, dass die Codequalität mit jedem Release besser wird. Dabei bleibt das Produkt im Einsatz: Wartung, Support und neue Features laufen parallel zur Modernisierung.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Legacy-Module bei laufendem Betrieb schrittweise durch Symfony-Services und React-Oberflächen ersetzen

  • Fullstack-Features von der Datenbank bis zum Frontend entwickeln, teils auch als kundenspezifische Erweiterungen

  • Bestehenden Legacy-Code pflegen, debuggen und weiterentwickeln

  • Code-Reviews durchführen und die Testabdeckung ausbauen

  • Mit Entwicklungsleitung und Geschäftsführung abstimmen, welche Bereiche als Nächstes modernisiert werden

  • Unsere zwei Auszubildenden im letzten Ausbildungsabschnitt fachlich begleiten (ohne disziplinarische Führung)

  • Gelegentlich an Kundenterminen teilnehmen, etwa alle 3–4 Wochen

Nach 6 Monaten …

… setzt du Features eigenständig um, hast spürbar zur Modernisierung beigetragen, die Codequalität verbessert und bist für unsere Azubis eine feste Ansprechperson.

Dein Profil

  • Erfahrung: etwa 4–5 Jahre in der professionellen Softwareentwicklung (ein Richtwert, keine harte Grenze)

  • PHP: fundierte Kenntnisse in modernem PHP 8.x mit objektorientierter Architektur, etwa Dependency Injection, Interfaces und SOLID

  • Symfony: nachweisbare Praxiserfahrung mit dem Framework

  • Legacy-Code: Du gehst sicher mit gewachsenen Codebasen um. Du refaktorierst, debuggst und entwickelst weiter, ohne alles neu zu schreiben.

  • JavaScript/React: solide Erfahrung im Frontend, jQuery schreckt dich nicht ab

  • Datenbanken: relationale Datenbanken wie MySQL/MariaDB oder SingleStore und sicherer Umgang mit SQL

  • Tooling: Git und Arbeit mit CI/CD

  • Sprache: Deutsch auf C1-Niveau, Englisch mindestens B1

  • Arbeitsweise: eigenständig, strukturiert, proaktiv und mit hohem Qualitätsanspruch

  • Persönlich: Du kommunizierst verlässlich, arbeitest gern im Team, übernimmst Verantwortung, hast keine Angst vor schwierigen Codestellen und gibst dein Wissen gern weiter.

  • Abschluss: Ausbildung oder FH-Abschluss zählen bei uns genauso viel wie ein Uni-Studium. Entscheidend ist deine Praxiserfahrung.

Pluspunkte: REST/API-Design und Schnittstellenentwicklung, automatisiertes Testing (PHPUnit, Jest), Docker, Deployment-Pipelines und Cloud, Software-Architektur und Design

-

Patterns, produktiver Einsatz von KI-Tools wie Claude Code oder Codex. Erfahrung mit Software für den öffentlichen Sektor ist nicht nötig.

Dein Team

Ein kleines Team mit kurzen Wegen: Daniel (Developer Lead), Nico (Geschäftsführer & Projektmanager), der selbst aktiv mitentwickelt, ein externer Entwickler und zwei Auszubildende. Ihr stimmt euch täglich ab. Daniel und Nico übernehmen dein Onboarding persönlich.

So läuft der Bewerbungsprozess

  1. Kennenlerngespräch mit Sara

  3. Teamgespräch vor Ort

  4. Angebot

Über Girona

Seit über 25 Jahren entwickelt die Girona Softwareentwicklung GmbH in Berlin Software für die öffentliche Verwaltung. Städte wie Berlin, München, Bonn und Dessau setzen seit Jahrzehnten auf unsere Lösungen, Konsentas etwa in Bürgerämtern, Gesundheitsämtern sowie Kfz-Zulassungs- und Führerscheinstellen.

description:
About Wolt

At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we're building the delivery of (almost) everything and you'll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.

Working at Wolt isn't always easy, but it's definitely exciting. Here you'll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You'll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you're a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.

About the Team

Our Infrastructure teams build the foundation that engineers at Wolt, Deliveroo, and DoorDash build on: the compute, cloud, and networking capabilities that enable Engineering teams to develop, deploy, and run services at global scale. The EU Compute team has a specific focus on provisioning, scaling, and the efficient operation of GPU infrastructure for AI and ML workloads. This is an emerging space with plenty of greenfield opportunities.

We're looking for a Staff Engineer to be a hands-on technical leader for this infrastructure work that crosses team and brand boundaries. You'll set direction for the platform, turn complex problems into deliverable plans, write and review production code, and help other engineers make sound decisions. It's an exciting time to join: we're building a global platform and the choices made now will shape how engineers across the company ship for years.

What you'll be doing

You'll own some of the hardest infrastructure problems in the company and make the platform easier to operate and safer to build on. We're determined to build great platform products and user experiences, and you'll be pivotal in making this reality.

Day-to-day in this role you'll:

  • Set technical direction for shared AWS and Kubernetes infrastructure, balancing reliability, security, developer experience, and cost.
  • Lead substantial initiatives from design through rollout and operation, coordinating dependencies and decisions across Wolt, Deliveroo and DoorDash, focusing on workloads targeting GPUs.
  • Evolve Kubernetes clusters, cloud networking, identity, and infrastructure provisioning to support growing and varied workloads.
  • Build reusable Terraform patterns and self-service tooling that help teams provision infrastructure safely and consistently.
  • Improve deployment and operational practices, including GitOps, observability, capacity planning, incident response and recovery.
  • Use production signals and developer feedback to find platform friction, choose where to invest and measure whether changes actually help.
  • Assist with supporting the platform, with deep focus on GPU infrastructure, as well as broad focus on compute in general.
  • Gracefully sunset legacy infrastructure and tooling, and create strategies to reduce toil.
  • Mentor engineers through design reviews, implementation and incidents, raising the quality of infrastructure work across teams.

Our humble expectations

  • Deep experience building and operating Kubernetes and AWS infrastructure in production. Familiarity with GPU workloads and orchestration is a plus.
  • Strong software engineering skills: you use Go, Python or a similar language to build maintainable tools and automation.
  • Experience with infrastructure as code (we use Terraform) and with designing systems that other engineering teams depend on.
  • A track record of leading complex technical work across teams, including architectural decisions, delivery, and operational follow-through. You have the breadth to collaborate and design across team and domain boundaries, and the depth to have hands-on impact.
  • Strong judgment on trade-offs in distributed systems, networking, security, reliability, and cloud cost.
  • Clear communication, and the ability to bring people together around a practical technical direction.

What we offer

  • Scope and influence. Shape infrastructure used globally, while staying close to the engineering. Your work will help product teams ship services with greater ease and confidence.
  • Real problems at global scale. Multi-cluster Kubernetes, AI / ML workloads, cloud networking, GitOps, and progressive delivery across a global company.
  • Autonomy and ownership. Set direction and see it through from design to operation, with the backing of a global engineering organisation spanning Europe and the US.
  • Growth. Room to expand your scope, whether through deeper technical leadership or broader cross-domain influence.
  • Great people. Work with talented engineers and leaders in a diverse, international environment, mentoring and learning from others.

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

We're committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That's why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

Our Global Structure


Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

About the role

We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead Codeless, our internal Server-Driven UI (SDUI) platform team. In this role, you will lead a cross-functional team bridging mobile/web frontend engineering and core platform backend systems.

While this role is deeply rooted in modern UI architecture, its mission goes beyond standard UI development: Codeless empowers product teams across the organization to ship dynamic, native UI experiences dynamically from the backend—eliminating app store release bottlenecks, dramatically accelerating feature iteration, and establishing a unified UI schema across iOS, Android, and Web.

What you'll be doing

This is a role with broad impact, from hands-on technical guidance to championing web and mobile accessibility across the company. We're looking for a leader who excels at fostering collaboration and can confidently guide a concept from initial idea to robust implementation.

Day-to-day in this role you'll:

  • Team Leadership & Strategy: Build, mentor, and scale an engineering team responsible for our core Server-Driven UI platform ("Codeless"). Foster an inclusive, high-ownership engineering culture.
  • Platform Architecture & Evolution: Oversee the design and evolution of dynamic layout engines, declarative UI schemas, and client rendering frameworks across iOS, Android, and Web.
  • Developer Velocity & Platform Adoption: Partner with product feature teams to drive internal adoption of Codeless. Ensure the platform provides exceptional Developer Experience, clear tooling, robust design system integration, and seamless debugging workflows.
  • Technical Execution & Quality: Set high technical standards for platform performance, payload optimization, caching strategies, backward compatibility, and graceful offline/fallback behavior across client devices.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with Product Managers, Design System leaders, and Core Infrastructure engineers to align the Codeless roadmap with broader company initiatives and global design paradigms.

What you'll need to thrive

Engineering Management: 3+ years of experience managing software engineering teams, with a track record of coaching engineers, delivering complex platform initiatives, and driving technical strategy.

UI & Platform Domain Expertise: Strong foundational background in mobile (iOS/Android) or modern web architecture (React, SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose, or declarative UI paradigms).

Product & Platform Mindset: Ability to treat internal product engineering teams as customers, evaluating platform success through developer velocity, adoption metrics, and rendering performance.

Why join us

At Deliveroo, you'll do work that matters—solving real-world problems in a three-sided marketplace that's constantly evolving. We're food lovers, problem solvers, community builders and more, brought together by a shared drive to make things better. Working here you can expect to:

🔧 Solve meaningful problems at real scale Work on a complex, always-on marketplace that impacts millions every day.

🌱 See your impact, fast Ship, test and improve ideas quickly in a low-hierarchy, high-ownership environment.

🧠 Grow through challenge and ownership Take on big, ambiguous problems and accelerate your career with strong support.

🌎 A culture built for builders High standards, collaboration, flexible working and continuous learning.

💰 Share in the success you help create Competitive salary and equity options, so you're rewarded for the impact you make.

➡️ Want a deeper look at how we build? Check out our Tech Blog.

We aim to create a fair process that lets your skills shine—our interview typically includes 3-4 stages. Explore our Engineering Interview Guide here to help you feel confident at each stage.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We're committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong.

We believe in equality of opportunity and welcome candidates from all backgrounds regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion, or belief.

If you have a disability or long-term health condition and need support to apply for one of our roles, or require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, you'll have the opportunity to let us know once you've submitted your application. We'll share details on how to request support so we can ensure you have a fair and equitable experience.

If you're excited about making a real impact in a fast-moving marketplace and growing your career alongside ambitious, supportive teams, we'd love to hear from you!


Beware of recruitment scams: DASH Brands will never ask you to pay money or share sensitive financial information during hiring — learn more about DASH Brands' legitimate recruiting process at careersatdoordash.com/recruitment-scam-awareness.

Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecrafts for humanity.

We are looking for an Avionics Systems Engineer to support the design, development, integration, and validation of spacecraft avionics systems. The role focuses on delivering robust and reliable electronic systems for data handling, communications, and control across all mission phases.

The engineer will contribute to system architecture definition, interface management, verification activities, and requirements engineering, while working closely with multidisciplinary teams and external stakeholders. In this role, you might be assigned to different avionics systems of the spacecraft.

Key Responsibilities

System Design & Architecture

  • Define and develop avionics system architectures, including electronics, data handling, and communication functions.

  • Ensure end-to-end consistency of data flows, interfaces, and system-level requirements.

  • Support selection and definition of avionics equipment, computing platforms, sensors, and communication hardware.

  • Contribute to spacecraft-level trade-offs between performance, reliability, mass, power, and cost.

Communications & Data Handling

  • Define onboard and ground-related communication and data handling concepts.

  • Support implementation of telemetry, telecommand, and data distribution architectures.

  • Ensure reliable data acquisition, processing, storage, and transmission under mission constraints.

  • Contribute to bandwidth, timing, and data budget analyses.

Integration & Interface Management

  • Define and manage interfaces between avionics and other spacecraft subsystems (power, propulsion, GNC, payload, etc.).

  • Ensure compatibility between spacecraft, launch vehicle, and ground segment interfaces.

  • Coordinate interface definitions with internal teams, suppliers, and external stakeholders.

External Regulatory & Certification Leadership

Strong ability to technically present, defend, and substantiate avionics subsystem designs and verification evidence with external regulatory and certification authorities, including NASA, ESA, and other government agencies, supporting spacecraft qualification, safety, and flight certification.

Verification & Validation

  • Define and support verification and validation strategies for avionics systems.

  • Participate in simulation, hardware-in-the-loop (HIL), and system-level testing activities.

  • Analyze test results, identify anomalies, and drive corrective actions.

  • Ensure compliance with system performance and reliability requirements.

Requirements Engineering

  • Capture, analyze, and manage system and subsystem requirements.

  • Ensure full traceability from mission objectives to implementation and validation.

  • Contribute to system documentation, including specifications, interface control documents, and test plans.

  • Ensure compliance with applicable space standards and engineering best practices.

Cross-functional Collaboration

  • Work closely with software, hardware, systems, operations, and mission engineering teams.

  • Participate in design reviews, technical exchanges, and system trade-off discussions.

  • Support alignment with external partners, suppliers, and customers.

  • Contribute to integration campaigns, launch preparation, and mission operations support.

Required Qualifications

  • Degree in Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Systems Engineering, or equivalent.

  • +7 years experience in avionics systems, electronics, embedded systems, or spacecraft engineering.

  • Strong understanding of:

    • Electronic and embedded system architectures

    • Communication and data handling principles

    • System integration and interface management

  • Experience with requirements engineering and system lifecycle development.

  • Knowledge of verification and validation methods, including testing and simulation.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

  • Ability to work in multidisciplinary engineering environments.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in spacecraft avionics or aerospace systems.

  • Familiarity with space communication and data standards (e.g., CCSDS).

  • Experience with HIL testing, simulation environments, or digital engineering tools.

  • Exposure to safety-critical or mission-critical system development.

  • Experience working in international or multi-stakeholder engineering teams.

description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecrafts for humanity.

About The Exploration Company

At The Exploration Company, we are developing, producing and operating Nyx, a modular and reusable orbital space vehicle that aims to eventually be refuelled in orbit, carrying cargo and potentially humans in the long run. The heart of a spacecraft lies in its engine, which is why we develop our own propulsion systems, aiming for the highest level of efficiency and reliability.

Role Summary

We are seeking a Junior Engine Control System & Monitoring Engineer to join the engine control and monitoring team of Storm, our high-thrust LOX/LCH4 cryogenic rocket engine. Working alongside senior control engineers, you will develop and test control and monitoring algorithms, work with the engine functional models provided by the functional team, contribute to setting up the controller development environment, and help verify the controller through Model-, Software- and Hardware-in-the-Loop testing and during engine test campaigns. This is an entry-level, hands-on role for a recent graduate with strong control fundamentals who wants to learn on real hardware and progressively grow into full ownership of safety-critical engine control functions.

Key responsibilities:

1. Control & Monitoring Algorithm Development

• Design and implement engine control and monitoring algorithms, following the software team's rules, guidelines and auto-coding practices.

• Contribute to the definition of the engine regulation strategy (thrust and mixture ratio control, chill-down, start-up and shutdown transients) together with functional and system engineers.

• Support the definition of control and monitoring requirements for engine subsystems (valves, pumps, sensors, controller, software).

2. Simulation & Controller Development Environment

• Contribute to setting up the controller development environment: toolchain, model and code configuration management, auto-coding chain, and the MiL/SiL/HiL simulation and test infrastructure.

• Integrate the engine functional models delivered by the functional team (turbopumps, valves, combustion devices, cryogenic feed lines; steady-state, transient and chill-down) into the control design and simulation environment, deriving simplified or linearised models for controller synthesis where needed.

• Run closed-loop simulations to assess controller performance, stability margins and robustness to model uncertainties.

• Feed test results back to the functional team to support model correlation, and flag model limitations that matter for control.

3. Health Monitoring & Fault Management

• Contribute to the engine monitoring strategy that assesses the health status of the engine and its subsystems (combustion chamber, turbopumps, valves…).

• Implement fault detection and sensor validation logic for both real-time protection and post-test analysis.

• Support failure mode analyses (FMEA) and the management of failure modes, paving the way for engine reusability.

4. Validation, Testing & Documentation

• Prepare and run Model-, Software- and Hardware-in-the-Loop (MiL, SiL, HiL) test campaigns to verify the control and monitoring functions at each step, from Simulink model to embedded code on target hardware.

• Support Storm engine and component cryogenic (LOX/LCH4) test campaigns: test preparation, on-site support, data processing and post-test analysis.

• Produce clear development documentation: specifications, test procedures, test reports and justification files.

What we would love to see from you:

• Master's degree (or equivalent) in Aerospace, Electrical, Control or Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

• Recent graduate (or graduating within the next months); no professional experience required. A master's thesis, internship or academic project in control, propulsion or embedded systems is a strong plus.

• Solid fundamentals in control theory, both classical and modern (state-space, robustness, digital control).

• Practical use of MATLAB/Simulink and Python through coursework or projects; basic knowledge of C/C++.

• Basic understanding of fluid dynamics and thermodynamics, and a strong interest in cryogenic propulsion and turbomachinery.

• Fluent in English.

Nice to Have:

• Exposure to MiL/SiL/HiL testing or real-time embedded systems.

• Experience with auto-coding from Simulink models.

• Familiarity with safety-critical design practices, reliability engineering or failure mode analysis.

• Interest or experience in data science applied to health monitoring and anomaly detection.

• Knowledge of space standards (ECSS, MIL-STD, NASA-HBK…).

• German and/or French.

Skills & Behaviours:

• Eagerness to learn and to take on increasing ownership under the guidance of senior engineers.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to draw useful conclusions from partial or contradictory data.

• Clear oral and written communication; comfortable working closely with engine, avionics, software and test teams.

• Organised, able to prioritise tasks and deliver within time constraints.

• Positive, flexible attitude and enthusiasm for space exploration.

• Behaviour consistent with The Exploration Company's core values of Mission, Vision, Integrity, Excellence and Teamwork.

Why you should join us!

What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is:  

  • We’re Agile - we make decisions fast whilst keeping our goals and systems in mind 

  • We’re Open and Collaborative - we are transparent about risks and obstacles, so that we can cooperate to overcome them  

  • We have a lot of Fun - we refuel our energy knowing we are democratising space. It’s a wonderful and rare opportunity, are YOU up for the challenge?  

We'd love to hear from you if you wish to be a part of our journey. Please submit your CV now for immediate consideration and we will be in touch shortly.

About Hiya

At Hiya, we’re making business calls more trusted, useful, and effective.

Voice remains one of the most important ways businesses communicate with their customers, but the value of a call depends on trust. When customers do not recognize who is calling or why, important conversations are missed, customer relationships suffer, and business outcomes are harder to achieve.

Hiya helps businesses create trusted calling experiences that benefit both sides of the conversation: enterprises can reach customers with confidence, and customers can answer with confidence. Our products support branded business calling, trusted caller identity, call performance insights, customer engagement, and voice security capabilities that help businesses strengthen relationships and improve outcomes.

This role sits in a core business area for Hiya and is focused on helping SMB and enterprise customers succeed.

About the Role

The engineering intern position is for an individual contributor who is responsible for architecting, implementing, and maintaining significant systems that serve hundreds of millions of requests per month. Hiya provides high-availability, latency-sensitive capabilities to telecoms, mobile apps, and other partners. In addition, you'll work with engineering teams across Hiya, some in Seattle and some in Europe, to define and deliver shared components and services. From day one, you will be paired with a dedicated mentor who provides structured guidance, technical feedback, and ongoing career mentorship.

What You'll Do

Design, code, and operate high-performance services and data processing pipelines on a modern technology stack, supported by a structured technical crash course during your first two weeks covering our core tools, architecture, and repositories.

Work at a supportive and fast-growing startup with a fantastic team, where you can collaborate with and learn from other great team members.

Make an impact in the lives of hundreds of millions of consumers.

Be supported in developing your skills and accelerating your career.

What We Are Looking For

  • Engineering: CS majors - 2nd year (graduating 2028)

  • Excitement to work on innovative technology advancements

  • A philosophy of iteration and continuous improvement

  • Working knowledge of building services that adhere to operational SLAs

  • A preference for velocity over perfection

  • A commitment to respectful and impactful collaboration

  • Self-motivated and excited to learn about new technologies

Our Interview Process: The Hiya Voice AI Challenge

Once we’ve confirmed your eligibility, you’ll receive the Hiya Voice AI Challenge by email-- a chance to build a working prototype of a voice-driven product in one of five tracks: Accessibility, Productivity, Creative Voice, Security, or Real-Time Assistance. You’ll have one week to build it, with optional virtual office hours along the way if you’d like to pitch your idea and get steering from our team first.

From there:

  • Submit and get reviewed. One of our engineers reviews your work. If we’d like to explore your project further, you’ll get a link to book a 30-minute virtual session with an engineer or two-- a quick demo, a walkthrough of your code, and some questions.

  • Final interviews, in person at Hiya. Candidates who advance join us for a final round in London (2nd & 3rd of December): a debugging/fixing session, a chance to add a feature to your own project, and a conversation about Hiya’s values.

AI tools are welcome and encouraged the whole way through.

What You Can Expect From Us

  • Dedicated technical mentorship with structured, regular feedback check-ins

  • Clear project scope and goals provided right at the start of your internship

  • Comprehensive onboarding to get you up to speed on Hiya's tooling, codebases, and systems quickly

  • A supportive, collaborative environment built on psychological safety and genuine impact

How We Work

Hiya is not a passive environment. We expect people to take ownership, form opinions, and engage directly with hard problems.

We work with a high degree of transparency and autonomy. Context is shared openly, and decisions are discussed, challenged, and then made. Once a call is made, we commit and move forward.

You'll be expected to work through ambiguity, weigh tradeoffs, and take responsibility for results, while keeping a high bar for quality and customer trust.

Every team member at Hiya is expected to live our core values:

  • Serve, our customers and partners by holding a high bar for trust and quality

  • Own, share in success and open up to failures

  • Lead, listen, show up with a point of view but commit entirely once a decision has been made

  • Improve, even if it means changing course or contradicting ourselves

  • Do, rather than observe

Come Work With Us!

We're building a team with diverse perspectives, identities, and professional experiences. We evaluate candidates through a business lens and believe that diversity and unique viewpoints make our company stronger, more dynamic, and a great place to build a career.

We've been recognized by Built In, GeekWire, Comparably, G2, Forbes, and Deloitte Technology Fast 500 for our culture, innovation, leadership, compensation, and more. At Hiya, we're a people-centric company focused on helping each employee grow both personally and professionally. We create a culture of support and empowerment that challenges the status quo, resulting in an energized team that's passionate about their work. You'll love working here if you're looking for an innovative challenge that's disrupting an industry. Come join us!

Hiya is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to building an inclusive environment for all employees.

About the Role:

Camunda's Revenue Operations organization is looking for a Senior GTM Systems AI and Automation Engineer to design, build and operate the AI-powered infrastructure that connects our go-to-market systems and removes manual work across Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, Partnerships and Account Development. You will join the GTM Systems team – a small group of builders who own a Salesforce-centric revenue stack – and take ownership of its AI and automation layer: agents, LLM integrations, MCP servers, retrieval pipelines, backend services and workflow orchestration. You will partner with GTM leaders to find high-impact problems, scope them, and ship reliable, well-governed solutions iteratively. This is a fully remote role and can be based anywhere we are eligible to hire.

What You Will Do:

  • Design, build and operate AI agents, LLM integrations and automations that connect Salesforce, Gainsight, Slack, Salesloft, Clari, HubSpot, Impartner and the rest of the GTM stack – reducing manual work across Sales, CS, Marketing, Partners and ADR teams.

  • Own the architecture of the GTM Systems AI layer: MCP servers, APIs, retrieval and context pipelines, reusable agent tools and skills, and serverless or containerized services on Google Cloud Platform (BigQuery, Cloud Run, Cloud Functions).

  • Ship production-grade LLM capabilities – prompt engineering, RAG, function calling, structured outputs, automated evaluations – with the guardrails to match: validation, fallback logic, confidence thresholds, human escalation paths, access controls, audit logging, and cost and latency management.

  • Partner with Revenue Operations, Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, Partnerships and SDR/ADR leaders to identify and prioritize automation opportunities, translate ambiguous requirements into maintainable solutions, and deliver incrementally with clear documentation.

  • Raise the engineering bar for the GTM Systems team: code review, automated testing, CI/CD, security governance, observability and technical documentation; mentor teammates on responsible AI-assisted development.

  • Design and deploy workflows on orchestration platforms such as Camunda and Clay, and create playbooks and enablement so GTM teams can use and operate automations independently.

What You Will Bring to the Role:

Must Haves:

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience (backend development, systems integration, data or analytics engineering, or automation), including at least 2 years shipping LLM or AI capabilities into production business workflows or internal tools.

  • Strong proficiency in Python and JavaScript/TypeScript (Node.js), with mature Git-based development habits: code review, automated testing, CI/CD.

  • Hands-on command of LLM patterns – prompt engineering, RAG, function/tool calling, structured outputs, model evaluation – and of their failure modes and mitigations (validation, fallback logic, confidence thresholds, human review, cost and latency control).

  • Experience integrating with Salesforce (REST/Bulk/Streaming APIs, data model, platform limits; Apex or Flow a plus) and other business systems via APIs and event-driven patterns, and with a cloud platform (GCP preferred: BigQuery, Cloud Run, Cloud Functions, IAM).

  • Ability to own a problem end-to-end with minimal guidance – scope, design, deliver, operate – and to communicate clearly with engineering and business stakeholders in a remote, asynchronous environment.

Nice to Haves:

  • Experience with the Model Context Protocol (MCP) or similar standards for connecting AI systems to tools and data; agent frameworks; vector databases or retrieval pipelines (pgvector, Pinecone, Weaviate, ChromaDB).

  • Exposure to AI observability and evaluation tooling (LangSmith, Weights & Biases, or custom eval frameworks).

  • Familiarity with orchestration platforms such as Camunda or Clay, and prior work in Revenue Operations, GTM Systems, Sales Operations or Marketing Operations in B2B SaaS.

  • Building lightweight interfaces for AI tools (React, Slack Block Kit, dashboards); Salesforce certifications (Platform Developer I/II, Integration Architect).

Equity: We also offer equity (where applicable) through our Virtual Stock Option Plan (VSOP).

Benefits & Perks

description:
Die Agentur PHILIPP GmbH ist eine mehrfach ausgezeichnete Technologie- und KI-Umsetzungsberatung für den Mittelstand. Wir entwickeln und implementieren KI-Lösungen, die im Alltag unserer Kunden funktionieren: von KI-Telefonie und Automatisierung über intelligente Dokumentenverarbeitung bis zu individuellen KI-Kollegen.

Wir machen aus KI keine Theorie. Wir übernehmen Verantwortung dafür, dass Lösungen sauber umgesetzt, integriert, getestet und vom Kunden wirklich genutzt werden.

Um unser Team weiter zu verstärken, suchen wir dich als DevOps Engineer für KI-Lösungen (m/w/d). Du sorgst dafür, dass unsere Anwendungen sicher bereitgestellt werden, zuverlässig laufen und sich kontrolliert weiterentwickeln lassen. Gemeinsam mit unserem Entwicklerteam schaffst du die technische Grundlage für einen stabilen Betrieb bei unterschiedlichen Kunden.

Aufgaben

  • Aufbauen, Betreiben und Weiterentwickeln unserer Hosting- und Deployment-Infrastruktur für KI-Anwendungen, Schnittstellen und Automatisierungen

  • Automatisieren von Builds, Tests und Deployments über CI/CD-Pipelines

  • Einrichten und Verwalten containerisierter Anwendungen sowie sauber getrennter Entwicklungs-, Test- und Produktionsumgebungen

  • Standardisieren und Dokumentieren von Infrastruktur und Konfigurationen nach dem Infrastructure-as-Code-Prinzip

  • Aufbauen von Monitoring, Logging und Alarmierung, damit Fehler frühzeitig erkannt und nachvollzogen werden können

  • Umsetzen von Zugriffskonzepten, sicherem Secrets-Management und der technischen Trennung von Kundenumgebungen

  • Einrichten und regelmäßiges Überprüfen von Backups, Wiederherstellung und Rollback-Verfahren

  • Analysieren und Beheben von Betriebsstörungen gemeinsam mit dem Entwicklerteam sowie Ableiten dauerhafter Verbesserungen

  • Überwachen von Ressourcenverbrauch und Infrastrukturkosten und Verbessern von Leistung und Wirtschaftlichkeit

Qualifikation

  • Praktische Erfahrung im DevOps-Bereich, in der Systemadministration oder im Betrieb produktiver Softwareanwendungen

  • Sichere Kenntnisse in Linux, Docker und grundlegenden Netzwerkthemen wie DNS, TLS und Reverse Proxies

  • Erfahrung mit CI/CD-Pipelines, beispielsweise mit GitHub Actions oder GitLab CI

  • Erfahrung mit einer gängigen Cloud-Plattform oder dem Betrieb selbst verwalteter Serverumgebungen

  • Kenntnisse in Infrastructure as Code, beispielsweise mit Terraform oder Ansible

  • Erfahrung mit Monitoring, Logging, Backups und der systematischen Analyse von Störungen

  • Sicherer Umgang mit Skriptsprachen wie Bash oder Python

  • Verständnis für IT-Sicherheit und den verantwortungsvollen Umgang mit sensiblen Unternehmensdaten

  • Interesse an den betrieblichen Besonderheiten von KI-Anwendungen, etwa externen Modell-APIs, variablen Laufzeiten und nutzungsabhängigen Kosten

  • Strukturierte Arbeitsweise und die Bereitschaft, Probleme nicht nur kurzfristig zu beheben, sondern ihre Ursachen zu beseitigen

  • Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse

  • Hybrides Arbeitsmodell: Wir legen Wert auf persönliche Zusammenarbeit und arbeiten daher an 3 Tagen pro Woche gemeinsam im Büro. An den übrigen 2 Tagen besteht die Möglichkeit zum Homeoffice.

Benefits

  • Verantwortung für die Infrastruktur hinter echten KI-Lösungen im Mittelstand

  • Gestaltungsspielraum beim Aufbau einheitlicher Betriebs- und Sicherheitsstandards

  • Direkte Zusammenarbeit mit unserem Entwicklerteam und kurze Entscheidungswege

  • Raum für Automatisierung und technische Verbesserungen, die den Arbeitsalltag des gesamten Teams erleichtern

  • Moderner Arbeitsplatz in Dingolfing (84130)

Unsere Haltung

Verstehen

Bevor wir etwas bauen, wollen wir das Unternehmen, die Menschen und die täglichen Abläufe wirklich verstehen. Wir versetzen uns in die Rolle unserer Kunden und fragen nicht zuerst, was technisch möglich ist, sondern was im Alltag wirklich hilft.

Nur dann entstehen Lösungen, die nicht am Bedarf vorbeigehen, sondern genutzt werden, Aufwand reduzieren und Probleme tatsächlich lösen.

Anpacken

Wir übernehmen Verantwortung und bleiben dran, bis der Job erledigt ist. Wir sprechen Probleme offen an, schaffen Klarheit und lösen sie, statt sie weiterzureichen.

Nicht alles läuft sofort glatt. Entscheidend ist, dass wir handeln, uns Hilfe holen, wenn sie nötig ist, und den Extra-Meter gehen, wenn es für den Erfolg unserer Kunden notwendig ist.

Liefern

KI ist für uns kein Selbstzweck. Gute Ideen, Konzepte oder Präsentationen reichen nicht.

Entscheidend ist, dass eine Lösung im Alltag funktioniert, verlässlich eingesetzt werden kann und für unsere Kunden einen echten Unterschied macht. Wir werden nicht dafür bezahlt, über Möglichkeiten zu sprechen. Wir werden dafür bezahlt, Ergebnisse zu liefern.

Besser werden

Wir haben einen hohen Anspruch an unsere Arbeit und wissen gleichzeitig, dass man nie auslernt. Wir testen, lernen, holen Feedback ein und denken über den ersten Lösungsansatz hinaus.

Fehler passieren. Entscheidend ist, dass wir sie offen ansprechen, daraus lernen und sie nicht zweimal machen. So werden unsere Lösungen, unsere Zusammenarbeit und unser Anspruch jeden Tag besser.

Unser Bewerbungsprozess

  1. Kurzbewerbung mit Lebenslauf und kurzer Beschreibung deiner bisherigen Infrastruktur- und Betriebsverantwortung

  2. Erstgespräch zum gegenseitigen Kennenlernen

  3. Praxisnahes Gespräch mit Geschäftsführung und Entwicklerteam

  4. Angebot

Klingt nach dir? Dann bewirb dich jetzt.

Wir freuen uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen.

We are looking for a Senior Data Engineer (f/m/d) at LIQID, who will play a pivotal role in building and scaling data infrastructure that powers decision-making.

This is not a role where you preserve what already exists. It is a role where you build what comes next. As LIQID scales beyond €4 billion in assets under management, the demands on our data infrastructure are growing fast. You will have real ownership over how we meet that challenge, with the autonomy to propose solutions and the backing to ship them.

 

What will keep you challenged?

  • Design, build, and optimize scalable data pipelines and storage solutions that ensure efficient, secure, and reliable data processing from source systems to our data warehouse

  • Develop and manage ETL/ELT workflows to integrate data from multiple sources, ensuring seamless ingestion, transformation, and availability

  • Implement and enforce data quality, validation, and monitoring processes to guarantee accuracy and integrity for analytics and operational use cases

  • Ensure data security and compliance by applying best practices and industry standards for handling sensitive information

  • Collaborate with analysts, product managers, and engineers to understand data needs and deliver solutions that unlock new insights

What you bring

  • Experience with cloud data platforms (e.g., AWS, Google Cloud) and modern data pipeline tools (e.g., Airflow, dbt)

  • FinTech experience is a plus, but a strong interest in financial services and data-driven decision-making is essential

We offer our clients financial peace of mind through exceptional, curated investment solutions – ranging from the world’s best private equity and venture funds to award-winning wealth management solutions. With over €4 billion in assets, we are backed by leading investors from the digital, private equity, and wealth management space, including LGT, Toscafund, HQ Trust, and Project A.
